title: Tenant-aware anomaly scoring + notification routing for console usage pipelines
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: We currently lack a reliable, tenant-aware anomaly detection and alerting flow for usage/cost/latency metrics in the Console. Ops and SREs are getting noisy or late signals; customers are occasionally surprised by billing spikes that were not surfaced quickly. Goal: build a streaming anomaly scoring layer that operates on per-tenant time series, supports rule-based and model-based detectors, deduplicates alerts, and routes notifications to the right on-call / billing contacts with sensible suppression and escalation policies. Deliver a Console UI surface for alert history and a lightweight API for suppressing and acknowledging incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming scorer produces anomaly scores for usage/cost/latency per-tenant within 60s of event arrival
Anomaly store in ClickHouse supports fast queries for last 30 days and powers Console incident list
Alert routing uses tenant metadata to map to PagerDuty service / Slack channel / billing-owner email
False-positive rate < 10% on historical test prompts and allows sensitivity tuning per-tenant
Backfill job reprocesses up to 7 days of late-arriving events and marks reprocessed alerts
On-call suppression window and dedup window configurable; UI shows suppressed alerts and reason
design_notes: Pipeline: Kafka -> Flink (windowed aggregations + feature extraction) -> Flink scoring operators -> ClickHouse / event topic
Detectors: hybrid approach — short-window rules (absolute thresholds and growth-rate) + LSTM-lite anomaly model for seasonality-aware residuals
Per-tenant baselines: maintain rolling-percentile baseline (p50/p90) + adaptive smoothing to avoid churn for small tenants
Routing: use tenant metadata service to resolve routing (pagerduty_id, slack_workspace, billing_contact). Fall back to global team route if unavailable
Dedup & suppression: implement fingerprinting (metric, tenant, hash(window_start, anomaly_type)) and a 30m dedupe TTL; suppression reasons persisted to ClickHouse
Observability: instrument scoring latency, model drift (model score distributions), and downstream delivery success/failure metrics
Privacy: avoid sending raw customer identifiers in alert payloads to Slack; include internal tenant-id only in PagerDuty payloads behind SSO
tradeoffs_and_choices: We chose Flink for low-latency windowed state and exactly-once semantics; alternative (Beam/Dataproc) had higher operational lift for tight latency requirements
LSTM-lite adds complexity but reduces FPs for tenants with weekly seasonality. For tiny tenants we fall back to simple rules to avoid noisy models
ClickHouse chosen for fast analytic reads for the Console despite higher storage cost vs BigQuery; Console needs sub-second incident list queries
Routing via tenant metadata service centralizes mapping but adds dependency; fallback routing table cached in service to reduce outage blast radius
implementation_plan: Spike: prototype Flink scoring job + local ClickHouse dev cluster (done)
Build: production Flink job with state backend on S3 + checkpointing; schema for anomaly events in ClickHouse
Integrate: tenant routing enrichment service call from scorer; implement safe timeouts and circuit breaker
Alerts: wire to PagerDuty and Slack integrations; create subscription config per-tenant in Console
UI: Console incident list + suppression controls; API to ack/suppress/resolve
Backfill: Spark job to rescore historical windows and mark reprocessed alerts
QA: run on staging with sampled tenants, tune sensitivity, run canary on 10% of traffic
Rollout: gradual ramp with auto-fallback and kill-switch
risks: Model drift: changes in customer behavior may increase FPs/TPs. Mitigation: daily drift detection job and auto-notify ML team
Late-arriving data: can cause duplicate alerts when backfills run. Mitigation: fingerprinting + backfill marker flags to dedupe
Operational complexity: Flink state and ClickHouse ops add SRE burden. Mitigation: run initial pipeline on managed Flink cluster and keep ops playbook
Privacy/regulatory: shipping cost data to third-party slack could be sensitive. Mitigation: mask identifiers and allow per-tenant redaction policy
